text:
Alice: thinking out loud — we need a concrete plan for preserving customer source IPs if we move to a shared regional relay instead of per-customer peering
Ben: agree, preserves IP is the blocker for a lot of customers (esp. security teams)
Carol: one option i ran locally: eBPF on the regional relay hosts to rewrite skb->dst and do DNAT so we don't need an ENI per tenant. lightweight, low cost.
Dan: eBPF sounds cool but operational surface area spikes. who handles route leaks, iptables fallback, kernel compat matrix?
Eva: +1 to Dan. also thinking about TLS termination model. if we do SNI passthrough we keep client certs intact, but we lose observability on payloads for routing decisions.
Alice: tradeoffs: per-tenant ENI = predictable source IP (customer sees stable src), but expensive and slow to onboard. shared-relay + ephemeral IP leases = cheap but harder to guarantee stability during failover.
Ben: can we do hybrid? per-customer ENI for enterprise with contract, shared for self-serve. default to shared with opt-in stable-ip.
Carol: hybrid is reasonable. eBPF approach allows sticky source ip by mapping a stable virtual IP -> tenant via L3/L4 rewrite. on failover we re-bind IP quickly.
Dan: re-bind quickly implies a central lease service + health probes. what about cross-AZ failover? ARP/neighbor cache timing will bite us. need ip-grace windows.
Eva: we should sketch failure modes. e.g. relay host crash, IP floating to new host, packets in flight from customer -> TCP resets. app-level retries might hide this but not always.
Alice: list of constraints to cover in RFC follow-up:
- preserve stable egress IP per enterprise when requested
- failover should aim for <5s of disruption or clear rollback plan
- no kernel module changes; must work on supported distros
- cert/key ownership cannot be forced to relay host for regulated tenants

Ben: also add metrics/costs:
- cost delta: ENI-per-tenant adds ~ $X/mo per tenant (ballpark)
- relay host pool + ephemeral IPs add network + NAT cost but lower fixed infra
- operational cost for eBPF debugging unknown, add 20% margin

Carol: prototyping notes I posted earlier:
```
# rough prototype sequence
1) relay receives conn, looks up tenant by SNI/header
2) allocate virtual src IP from tenant pool
3) install eBPF rewrite rule for 60s, attach to socket
4) forward to customer endpoint
```
This worked for HTTP keepalive tests, not yet for long-lived gRPC streams.

Dan: long-lived streams are the kicker — KV caching/stateful sessions will break if we flip IP mid-stream. so for those tenants we should require pinned pathways (ENI or dedicated relay shard).

Eva: auth model: prefer mTLS termination on customer side. relay can do SNI passthrough and route by ALPN/header. for telemetry we can sample at ingress with a redacted peek.

infra-bot: perf-test job queued: relay-ebpf-proto-2026-03-23 (ETA 30m) :gear:

Alice: next steps:
- Carol to draft mini-RFC outlining eBPF prototype + failover design (including lease service plan) by end of week
- Ben to run cost spreadsheet comparing ENI vs shared-relay across 100/1000 tenants
- Dan to list operational runbooks and kernel compatibility matrix
- Eva to enumerate compliance/regulatory blockers for TLS termination models

Ben: i'd also like a quick P0 checklist for enterprise customers who sign up early — what to offer them (ENI vs SLA-backed stable-ip).

Carol: adding that to draft. will include a table: workload type -> recommended path (grpc/long-lived -> ENI; request/response -> shared+lease).

Alice: thanks — keep this thread for RFC comments. ping me when draft ready.
Carol: will post draft link here when done.
Ben: :thumbsup:
